record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.context_brief: deriving exponential inequalities from expansion formulas
record.original_question: Can the spectral inequalities tr(exp(A + B)) <= tr(exp(A)exp(B)), tr(exp(A)exp(A^T)) <= tr(exp(A + A^T)), and lambda_max(exp(A)exp(A^T)) <= lambda_max(exp(A + A^T)) be derived directly from one of the matrix-exponential formulas (3.8), (3.9), or (3.10)? The source identifies this as an open route for explaining inequalities (3.13)-(3.15) from structural exponential expansions.

evidence.quote: An interesting open question that immediately arises is whether or not it is possible to derive (3.12)-(3.15) directly from any of the formulas (3.8), (3.9) or (3.10).
In this regard (3.10) appears to be the most promising candidate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $n\ge 1$ and let $A,B\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with $A,B$ Hermitian (so that $A+B$ and $\exp(A)\exp(B)$ make sense and the relevant traces and eigenvalues are real). For a square matrix $M$, write $\mathrm{tr}(M)$ for its trace, $\lambda_{\max}(M)$ for the largest (real) eigenvalue when it exists, $M^{T}$ for the transpose, and $\exp(M)=\sum_{k\ge 0} M^{k}/k!$ for the matrix exponential.

Three classical structural identities for the matrix exponential of a sum are available:

(F1) The Lie–Trotter product formula:
$$\exp(A+B)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\bigl(\exp(A/m)\exp(B/m)\bigr)^{m}.$$

(F2) The Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff series:
$$\exp(A)\exp(B)=\exp\!\Bigl(A+B+\tfrac12[A,B]+\tfrac1{12}[A,[A,B]]-\tfrac1{12}[B,[A,B]]+\cdots\Bigr),$$
where $[X,Y]=XY-YX$.

(F3) The Feynman/time-ordered "disentangling" identity:
$$\exp(A+B)=\exp(A)\,\mathcal{T}\exp\!\Bigl(\int_{0}^{1}e^{-tA}Be^{tA}\,dt\Bigr),$$
or equivalently
$$\exp(A+B)=\exp(A)+\int_{0}^{1}\exp\!\bigl((1-s)(A+B)\bigr)\,B\,\exp(sA)\,ds.$$

Three inequalities of interest are:

(I1) Golden–Thompson: for all Hermitian $A,B$,
$$\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\exp(A+B)\bigr)\;\le\;\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\exp(A)\exp(B)\bigr).$$

(I2) For every real square matrix $A$,
$$\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\exp(A)\exp(A^{T})\bigr)\;\le\;\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\exp(A+A^{T})\bigr).$$

(I3) For every real square matrix $A$,
$$\lambda_{\max}\bigl(\exp(A)\exp(A^{T})\bigr)\;\le\;\lambda_{\max}\bigl(\exp(A+A^{T})\bigr).$$

Question. Can the three inequalities (I1), (I2), (I3) be derived directly — by purely algebraic/analytic manipulation, without invoking auxiliary tools such as the Lieb concavity theorem, log-majorization, or analytic interpolation arguments — from one of the structural expansion formulas (F1), (F2), or (F3)? In particular, does formula (F3) admit a term-by-term comparison that yields each of (I1)–(I3)?
artifact.status_search_result: The Golden–Thompson inequality (I1) has many known proofs (Lie–Trotter plus log-majorization, complex interpolation, pinching, etc.), but the specific question of whether all three inequalities (I1)–(I3) can be obtained as direct consequences of a single structural expansion formula such as Lie–Trotter, Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff, or the Feynman/time-ordered disentangling identity does not appear to have a definitive resolution in the literature. The inequalities (I2)–(I3) involving $A$ and $A^{T}$ are less standard and no derivation explicitly via these expansion formulas was located. Status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Golden-Thompson inequality --- historical aspects and random matrix applications
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Golden-Thompson inequality proofs and history; standard proofs use Lie-Trotter combined with log-majorization or complex interpolation, not a single direct expansion-formula derivation.
status_evidence.claim: No standard proof derives the inequality directly from a single structural expansion formula in the sense asked.

status_evidence.title: Golden–Thompson inequality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Lists known proofs and generalizations of the Golden-Thompson inequality but does not record a direct derivation from BCH or the Feynman disentangling formula yielding the related transpose inequalities.
status_evidence.claim: The literature catalog does not include a unified derivation of the three inequalities from a single expansion formula.
